column1: What is the primary phonemic organizing principle of the Russian consonant system?
column2: The hard-soft (palatalization) contrast: most consonants form paired sets distinguished by whether the tongue blade is raised toward the hard palate (soft) or not (hard).

column1: In Russian orthography, how is consonant palatalization typically signaled?
column2: Through vowel letter choice (e.g., я, е, ё, ю, и signal a preceding soft consonant; а, э, о, у, ы signal a preceding hard consonant) rather than diacritical marks.

column1: What causes the 'fleeting vowel' (беглые гласные) alternation seen in день vs. дня?
column2: It is the synchronic reflex of Proto-Slavic jers (ĭ/ŭ): the jer vocalized in strong position (stressed/closed syllable) and deleted in weak position (before a vowel-initial suffix), per Havlík's Law.

column1: What is the operative rule for predicting fleeting vowel appearance in a Russian morpheme?
column2: A fleeting vowel surfaces when the morpheme ends in a closed syllable with no following vowel-initial suffix, and disappears when a vowel-initial suffix follows (avoiding an illegal coda cluster).

column1: What three grammatical categories intersect with Russian's six-case system to determine noun inflection?
How does animacy affect accusative case marking in Russian?
column2: Animate masculine singular nouns and all animate plurals syncretize their accusative form with the genitive, while inanimate nouns keep accusative identical to nominative.

column1: What case do the numerals два/три/четыре (2-4) govern, versus пять (5) and above?
column2: Два/три/четыре govern genitive singular; пять and above govern genitive plural.

column1: What is the core semantic distinction between Russian perfective and imperfective aspect?
column2: Perfective presents an action as a bounded, complete whole with achieved telos ('What happened?'); imperfective presents the action's internal unfolding as process, habit, or ongoing state, agnostic to completion ('What was/used to happen?').

column1: What are the two primary morphological strategies for forming perfective/imperfective aspectual pairs?
column2: Prefixation (perfectivizes an imperfective base) and suffixation (secondarily imperfectivizes a prefixed perfective while retaining the prefix's semantic modification).

column1: Why is Russian word order considered 'free' yet still structured?
column2: Because case morphology (not position) encodes grammatical relations, freeing word order to encode information structure (topic vs. focus) — Russian is discourse-configurational with canonical SVO as the neutral base order.

column1: In the sentence pair Студент прочитал книгу / Книгу прочитал студент, what remains invariant across all six word-order permutations?
column2: The case marking (nominative on студент, accusative on книгу), which unambiguously signals grammatical roles regardless of linear position.

column1: What are the three foundational invariants of Russian derivational morphology?
column2: 1) Root primacy principle (every complex word has an identifiable lexical root), 2) Semantic compositionality constraint (meaning is predictable from constituent morphemes), 3) Morphophonological interface (derivation triggers vowel-zero alternations, consonant mutations, and stress shifts to preserve phonotactics).
